state.question: Why does the pendulum period show genuine high-frequency scatter (σ ≈ 0.013 beats) around a stable mean, with no repeating sequences and no systematic drift, when a well-maintained mechanical pendulum should exhibit much lower variance and some serial correlation?

hypotheses.label: Instrumental noise: legitimate thermal, mechanical, and air-current fluctuations at the sensitivity limit of the measurement apparatus
hypotheses.rationale: The scatter is real, unsystematic, and free of pathological patterns (no exact repeats, no level shifts, no clustering). A 10-day baseline with n=72 trials and σ ≈ 0.013 is consistent with a well-designed experiment operating at its resolution floor. The fact that all 72 values are distinct and minimum spacing is 0.000063 suggests measurement resolution in the microbead range—typical of precision pendulum work. No drift or seasonal effect is visible. This is the most parsimonious reading: we have built a good apparatus and are now observing its honest noise floor.

hypotheses.label: Undetected periodic or quasi-periodic environmental modulation (e.g., building vibration, diurnal temperature cycling, operator technique drift) with period > 10 days or irregular amplitude
